name: CA-47
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 6 points on the PVI
Incumbent Dave Min has a large financial advantage ($3.4M raised vs $0.4M)
Prediction markets price Min at 95-96% to win
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Min: a D+6 seat, incumbency, and a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge, while both Kalshi and Polymarket price his win odds at 95% or higher. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Min underperforming the district's lean, or a surge of outside spending for Le Roux, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dave Min, a first-term Democratic incumbent, defends a coastal Orange County district that voted about six points more Democratic than the country in recent cycles. He enters the general with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $3.4 million to Jenny Le Roux's $376,000, and holds nearly $1.9 million in cash on hand against her $129,000. Outside spending has been negligible on both sides.

No public general-election polls are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, money, and markets, where Kalshi and Polymarket both give Min about a 95% chance of winning. Le Roux, a moderate local official, would need an unusual environment shift to close a gap this wide.
